title: Map everything the harness sends into a Claude session, annotated by source

brief.why:
Sameer, 2026-08-28: 'I really want to understand a bit more deeply what goes into your environment.' This repo maps the harness's AFFORDANCES across surfaces (what a session can DO where); this is the complementary axis — its INPUTS (what a session is TOLD, and by whom). Nobody has a byte-level account of it, and the estate makes decisions that depend on one: what earns residence in the always-loaded corpus (the ~/.claude carte board's whole intake question), what a context reading means, what an experiment holds constant. Progenitor: the infra GLM cost-per-task rig (bon iw-bepami) needed to know what an arm receives, and the method fell out of that.

What the first pass already established, on ONE headless probe (CC 2.1.251, cwd a notes clone): total request 290,624 B, splitting system 8,846 B (3.0%) / tools 97,780 B (33.6%, 37 schemas) / messages 183,532 B (63.2%). The CLAUDE.md corpus is NOT in the system prompt — it arrives as a 143,483-char <system-reminder> in the first user message, opening '# claudeMd ... These instructions OVERRIDE any default behavior', and it carries the user-level corpus AND the repo's own root CLAUDE.md together. A separate 34,407-char message with role 'system' carries the SessionStart hook output. So roughly a third of every turn is tool documentation and two thirds is instruction.
brief.what: 1. Capture an interactive multi-turn session against the dump server in a normal repo, via hublot 2. Build an annotator that attributes payload bytes to source files/mechanisms and reports the unattributed remainder 3. Produce the artefact for Sameer: a plain-English account of what a session is told and by whom, with the byte/token budget per source 4. Compare surfaces — headless vs interactive vs resumed — and note what differs 5. Write the durable knowledge into ~/notes/practices/harness-cartography/ per this repo's knowledge-vs-code boundary, keeping raw payloads out of git
brief.done: Sameer can read one document and see what goes into a session, where each part comes from, and what it costs — with the unattributed remainder stated rather than hidden, and every figure stamped with CC version and entrypoint
brief.how:
METHOD, proven — do not re-derive it. Stand a dump server in place of the model endpoint: it answers /v1/messages with a minimal valid Anthropic response so CC completes its turn, and writes every request body to disk. Working script and six captured payloads are preserved at ~/claude-corpus-archive/harness-payloads-2026-08-28/ (restic-backed, deliberately NOT git — they carry the whole corpus plus a metadata.user_id device id; keep any new captures out of git for the same reason). Point a session at it with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=any-string + ANTHROPIC_MODEL.

WHAT THE FIRST PASS COULD NOT SEE, and why a second is needed. The probe was `claude -p`, which is a different product surface, not a cheaper layer of the interactive one — the billing header block says so in the payload itself (cc_entrypoint=sdk-cli; an interactive run reads cli), and that string is the cheapest discriminator for which surface a capture came from. So capture INTERACTIVE via the hublot skill, multi-turn, in a NORMAL repo (not the experiment clone), to reach the injections a one-shot headless call structurally cannot produce: UserPromptSubmit hook output, the bon tactical step, total_tokens_reminder, skill_listing and deferred_tools_delta, the trust dialog on a fresh path, and whatever a resumed session does differently.

ATTRIBUTION is the actual deliverable and the harder half. For every byte, name the mechanism that put it there — match content against source files on disk and report byte ranges: which of ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, its @-imported context/*.md, each rules/*.md shard, the project CLAUDE.md, MEMORY.md, hook stdout, tool schemas (built-in vs plugin vs MCP server), gitStatus. Report unattributed remainder honestly rather than rounding it away — the residue IS the finding, because it is the part the harness generates that nobody on this estate wrote or can edit.

THREE TRAPS. (1) Do not infer the split by subtraction — the first pass nearly reported 'the corpus arrives in messages' having assumed tools were negligible, and tools are a third. Measure each key. (2) A capture is a claim about one session shape only; say which. (3) Numbers move with CC version — stamp every capture with the version and the entrypoint.

done_note: Superseded within a day of filing — the concordance arc delivered the substance in parallel (adjudicated with Sameer at the 2026-08-30 ceremony). Where each piece lives: the plain-English annotated account for Sameer = concordance v1 (infra tools/concordance, iw-rizapu, closed 2026-08-29); the reusable instrument (dump server, interactive capture under tmux, build.py annotator with provenance chips + token weights + unattributed-remainder honesty) = spm1001/variorum (var-rosogo). Residue NOT carried elsewhere: --what step 5, the durable write-through to ~/notes/practices/harness-cartography/ under this repo's knowledge-vs-code boundary — cart's next session should judge whether a pointer note suffices now that variorum owns the method.

title: Teach the scorer that a prediction has been adjudicated, so cell provenance stops diverging from the run file

brief.why: Discovered while working cart-mevefo (2026-08-30, adjudicating the two Gemini Notebook predictions). The scorer reads a run's report table and nothing else, so it still emits 'persistence | 2 | measured 2026-08-23' with the flag 'persistence rests on the canary prediction until the sweep verifies it' — correct on the day the run was written, and now stale: the sweep ran, the canary held, and the run file records provenance as 'measured 2026-08-23, re-verified 2026-08-30'. Two artefacts now disagree about the same cell, and the scored table is the one that gets plotted. Provenance discipline is this instrument's whole product (repo CLAUDE.md), so a silently stale provenance stamp is the defect it most needs not to have.
brief.what: 1. Parse a run file's Predictions section into (prediction, due date, verdict, verdict date) 2. Let an adjudicated prediction update the provenance stamp and retire the flag it answers 3. Refuse to invent a verdict date — an unadjudicated prediction must keep the flag 4. Fixture test over the gemini-notebook run, which has one held canary and one correctly-absent sleeper
brief.done: Scoring the 2026-08-23 Gemini Notebook run emits persistence provenance 'measured 2026-08-23, re-verified 2026-08-30' without hand-editing, and a run whose predictions are still open still shows the flag.
brief.how: The fix is a parse target, not a special case: predictions and their verdicts are already written in a consistent shape in the run files ('## Predictions to test', one bullet per prediction, verdict sub-bullets opening 'Verdict YYYY-MM-DD — '). Parse those and let an adjudicated prediction upgrade the provenance date and clear the matching 'rests on the prediction' flag. Resist hardcoding the canary: the sleeper prediction adjudicates too, and it bears on the same persistence cell from the other side (it caps the level rather than dating it). Worked example to test against: runs/gemini-notebook-2026-08-23.md now carries both.

title: Run the two dated Gemini Notebook checks: sleeper no-fire (~24 Aug), canary in Studio artifacts (~30 Aug)

brief.why: The 2026-08-23 run left two testable predictions (runs/gemini-notebook-2026-08-23.md §Predictions) and the loop that would have remembered them is paused — this bon is the calendar.
brief.what: 1. ~24 Aug: confirm NOTHING stirred in the notebook (the subject predicted its PID-1027 sleeper dies with the container — the correct result is absence) 2. ~30 Aug: canary-sweep.py picks up CANARY-gemini-notebook-2026-08 from the run file; verify canary.txt still sits in the notebook's Studio artifacts (artifactId 02177fd4-…) via passe/CDP 3. Upgrade the persistence cell provenance on both results
brief.done: Both predictions adjudicated in the run file with dates.
brief.badly: If we miss the real contours of the underlying Gemini harness.

done_note:
Both predictions adjudicated with dates in runs/gemini-notebook-2026-08-23.md (done criterion met). CANARY: HELD - canary.txt (artifactId 02177fd4-...) opened in tube's session Chrome and its body read back as CANARY-gemini-notebook-2026-08, seven days on. The list row was NOT accepted as evidence, and neither was a page-wide string test: the token also sits in the chat transcript, so includes() returns true either way (it did, and was discarded). Discriminator was the occurrence count rising 1->2 on opening the artifact, with the second occurrence localised to the viewer pane by a recorded text dump. SLEEPER: no wake-up effect reached the notebook - 4 of 4 artifacts present and all stamped 6d ago, no pagination in the panel, sources still 1, and the chat carries no turn after 23 Aug. Known-positive control stated beside the null: the same probe rendered the full 23 Aug transcript, the source, all four rows, and the canary's own body.

VERIFICATION: one fresh-context essayeur (fable) on Sameer's falsifier - 'If we miss the real contours of the underlying Gemini harness'. Returned SOUND WITH GAPS with four findings; all four folded in before this close. The one that mattered: my four-artifact baseline was checked against memory, not against this file's own Residue inventory, which named FIVE. Resolved rather than left open - the transcript's only named sync line is field-report-test.txt and the string 'field-rep' occurs in the whole transcript exactly twice, both that same file, so the fifth was one file double-counted under its UI-truncated name. Nothing was shed; Residue corrected in place, dated; durability strengthens to 4/4 rows persisted, 1/4 content-verified. Also folded: mechanism restated as effect (container death and 'no cron' are the subject's own account, never measured - the storage-not-residency claim holds without them); the chat channel demoted to corroboration because a detached bash process cannot mint a chat turn, so it could never have falsified; and the 'exactly'/'in the viewer pane' clauses grounded in the recorded dump rather than in session memory.

FOUND ALONG THE WAY: item 13 is defective as written - it accepted a wake action the subject elided ('sleep 86400 && ...'), and that ellipsis is the subject's own, recoverable nowhere. With no wake action on record the expected trace cannot be derived, so the prediction was strictly untestable. Letter v3 queue opened in instrument.md section 7 with three amendments.

SHIPPED repo-side: runners/gemini-notebook/read-artifact.py (trusted-click artifact reader; prints its own known-positive control; all four exit paths exercised, including refusing to report an absence when an open viewer hides the list) and README rules 5-6. Card step 3 (persistence provenance) done. Scorer re-run over the edited file: Freedom 11, unchanged; 13 tests green. FILED: ppt-zirehi on the passe board (the 23 Aug note cited 'passe-hefovo', which never existed - that board's prefix is ppt, so the gaps went unfiled for a week) and cart-hetiru (scorer provenance now diverges from the adjudicated run file). Notebook and all artifacts left in place; Residue now says explicitly that the sweep having run is NOT a licence to delete.
